clue.text: I rent pets or fish out

indicators.note: a fish out of water flails about, so these letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lets out their pets or takes their goldfish out of the tank.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter at the start looks like a Roman numeral or the setter, but it is the whole definition, read as a grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the pronoun used by the speaker about themselves is called the first person singular.

clue.text: Intoxicated Time news chief who acts before thinking?

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
someone impulsive is described as rash
the editor of a newspaper, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A drunken editor of Time magazine makes impulsive decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: Time looks like the magazine's name, but it is just the letter abbreviation; the rash quality is attached to the editor that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed is informal slang for very drunk, a common modern way of saying someone is wasted.

clue.text: Where we live the Man put up covering over Banksy's work?

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it, holding the other inside
in a down clue, putting something up reads its letters from bottom to top

parts.note: the man referred to by his pronoun
Banksy is a famous British street artist, so his work is art

explanation.surface: A man hangs a covering over a Banksy mural on the wall where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy is the anonymous British graffiti artist whose murals are sometimes covered or removed by property owners.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet Earth is the home of the human race, the place where all of us live.

clue.text: Bother at home with multi-function toilet?

parts.note: someone at home is in
a commode is a piece of furniture that may be a chest of drawers or a chair concealing a chamber pot

explanation.surface: A householder is troubled by a fancy toilet that does several jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: The commode earns 'multi-function' because the same word names both a chest of drawers and a chair with a pot hidden in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode someone is a formal verb meaning to cause them inconvenience or trouble them.

clue.text: What Hoskins does for work is kissing and canoodling (both topless)

indicators.note: topless means each word loses its top, which in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
amorous kissing and cuddling is called petting

explanation.surface: A cheeky confession that the setter's job amounts to topless snogging.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoskins is the setter of this puzzle, so his work is compiling crosswords. Both 'is' and the cuddling word lose their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Compiling crosswords is called setting, and a crossword compiler such as Hoskins is known as a setter.

clue.text: Old state publicity on southern island area enthrals American

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one part holds another inside it

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
S is the abbreviation for south or southern
I is the abbreviation for island
A is the abbreviation for area
US for American

explanation.surface: A publicity campaign for a southern island wins over an American visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the rest; the American goes inside that whole run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a German kingdom and state that was formally abolished after the Second World War.

clue.text: Those leading reviews examine academic delivering social studies

indicators.note: the ones leading are at the front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the initial letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Critics assess a lecturer who is teaching a course in social studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social studies' looks like a fixed phrase, but the last word is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university is the British way of saying you study it there.

clue.text: A lovebird in a frenzy can make an American colour

indicators.note: something in a frenzy flaps about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An agitated parrot flapping around produces a flash of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The dull greenish shade is best known as the colour of US Army uniforms and equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the khaki-green shade adopted by the United States military for uniforms and vehicles.

clue.text: Having eaten the last of entrée, try special nuts

indicators.note: whatever has eaten something holds it inside itself

parts.note: to try something out is to test it
S is an abbreviation for special

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of the French dish word

explanation.surface: After finishing the starter, a diner is urged to sample some special nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like a dish on the menu; it is slang for the male reproductive glands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is vulgar slang for testicles, and testes is the anatomical plural of testis.

clue.text: A price cut given to old, half-dry fruit

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only half of the two-letter abbreviation is kept

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
TT stands for teetotal, someone who is dry and drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A shop offers pensioners a discount on dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means abstaining from alcohol, which crosswords abbreviate as TT; half of that pair supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit, often sold dried, related to the peach and plum.

clue.text: A French Fancy with a filling that's different

indicators.note: a cake with a filling has something placed in its middle

parts.note: the French word for a or one
to fancy something is to like it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cake with an unusual filling stands out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A French Fancy is a small iced sponge cake sold in Britain; the cake name is split into an article and a verb. The A filling sits between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Unalike is an adjective meaning not similar, so two things that are unalike are different.

clue.text: My parts have an unpleasant smell, okay?

indicators.note: when something parts it splits and separates, so these letters come apart and are put back in a new order

parts.note: my as an exclamation of surprise, like oh
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A worried person asks whether their body has started to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My parts' reads as private parts, but 'My' is the exclamation. Hum is informal British for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum describes something merely mediocre and unexciting, middling rather than good, as a shrugged okay suggests.

clue.text: Playing tennis is, at first, terribly demanding

indicators.note: playing about with the letters moves them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter alone of the following word

parts.note: the initial letter of this word

explanation.surface: Playing tennis is very tiring and demanding at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' looks like an adverb on 'demanding', but only its first letter joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An insistent person keeps demanding something and will not take no for an answer.

clue.text: Too much Hoskins would upset? I agree completely!

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, excessive
the setter speaks of himself as I, so I'd is short for I would

explanation.surface: The setter admits that too many of his puzzles would annoy solvers, and a reader agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name in the third person; here Hoskins stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying ditto signals that the same applies to you too, an emphatic way of expressing complete agreement.

clue.text: I can't act stupidly around Independent strategist

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around another, enclosing it
doing something stupidly means getting it in the wrong order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: eight letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored
I is the abbreviation for Independent

explanation.surface: A wooden actor confesses that he cannot act around an independent political planner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is also the newspaper this puzzle comes from, which makes the abbreviation feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician plans moves cleverly to gain an advantage, just as a strategist does.

clue.text: Great dosh arranged for those looking after some kids?

indicators.note: arranging things puts them into a fresh order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Childminders are promised a big pay packet.
explanation.walkthrough: Kids reads as children, but young goats are kids too. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Goatherds tend flocks of goats, whose young are called kids, so they look after kids of a kind.

clue.text: Stoned? Wanting a rich stew? Stick a baby in it before eating?

definitions.text: Stick a baby in it before eating?

parts.note: someone stoned on drugs is high

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients up together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: five letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cannibal with the munchies fancies a rich baby stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The ghoulish reading has the baby as the meal; really the baby is simply seated before its own feed.
explanation.definitionFit: A highchair is a tall seat with a tray where an infant is placed to be fed at mealtimes.

clue.text: A conservative moron hedging over "abnormal union"

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so one word encloses another

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a cretin is an insulting word for a stupid person
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A Tory dimwit dodges questions about an unconventional marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase looks like a sneer at a relationship, but it is a medical sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine accretion is the growing together of parts that are normally separate, such as fused fingers.

clue.text: Give oxygen to a singer that has been gripped by drugs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something gripped is held tight between two others, so one part sits inside another

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so two of them are drugs
an informer who sings to the police is a rat

explanation.surface: Paramedics give oxygen to a pop star who has overdosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a musician, but in crime slang to sing is to inform, and an informer is a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate something is to introduce air, and thus oxygen, into it, as with soil or water.

clue.text: One cold with awful lice and small, frozen danglers?

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on a tap
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A shivering person with nits finds a certain small part of the body frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danglers' with a question mark hints at something rude, but these hang from roofs in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Icicles are spikes of frozen water that hang down from eaves and gutters in freezing weather.

clue.text: Clergyman touring pub raised, then nursed a tot?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters reads them from the bottom up
someone touring goes all the way around a place, enclosing it

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric in a cathedral
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A vicar on a pub crawl lifts a toddler and comforts it.
explanation.walkthrough: The tot looks like a small drink after the pub, but here it is a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny is to look after a young child as a nanny does, caring for and nursing it.

clue.text: Type of dance music found back in drab Baghdad

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from right to left
the answer is sitting inside the following words, spanning them

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A dull club in the Iraqi capital plays a style of dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabba is a fast, aggressive form of hardcore techno that originated in Rotterdam in the 1990s.

clue.text: Not all of part is terrible for Folies performer

indicators.note: only a portion of the words is used, a stretch lying inside them

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a Folies Bergère showgirl's role is partly dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Folies Bergère is a famous Paris music hall known for its cabaret revues.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer, typical of a Paris cabaret show.

clue.text: Are you texting people fed up with one's downfall?

indicators.note: fed up front, the following piece is supplied ahead of the larger word

parts.note: in text-message shorthand the words are written as two single letters
the Roman numeral for one
a people sharing a country form a nation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are texting people who have grown tired of your fall from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like being sick of something; read cryptically it puts the single letter ahead of the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is the state of being ruined, a collapse or fall from fortune, just like a downfall.

clue.text: Is Hoskins good not to take too many drugs, mate?

parts.note: the setter is I, so asking whether he is becomes am I

indicators.note: not taking something means leaving it out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
OD is short for overdose

explanation.surface: The setter asks a pal whether he is doing well to avoid an overdose.
explanation.walkthrough: With the setter standing for I, the question 'Is Hoskins?' becomes 'am I?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is used informally in English for a pal or mate.

clue.text: Trainee Indy setter about to get puzzle right … finally!

indicators.note: turned about, the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Dac was a long-serving setter for the Independent crossword

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter alone of each word

parts.note: the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A novice setter at the Independent finally gets a puzzle right.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indy is the Independent newspaper; crosswords sometimes clue their own setters by pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training to become an officer in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Nerd you and I must get in the sack (after some gyrating)

indicators.note: getting in means being placed inside the other word
gyrating means turning round, so the letters are spun to run the other way

parts.note: to hit the sack is to go to bed
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: A geek proposes that the two of you hop into bed after a bit of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The sack is slang for bed, as in hitting the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a boring, socially awkward or studious person, much the same as a nerd.

clue.text: Case full of French wine mostly, but no great shakes

indicators.note: something full of another holds it inside

parts.note: a court case is a trial

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: A crate packed with ordinary French wine turns out to be disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a box of bottles, but it is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: No great shakes is an idiom for unimpressive or unimportant, which is what trivial means.

clue.text: Hoskins is a German! Bit of surprise for those scanning docs?

parts.note: the setter is I, so Hoskins is becomes I'm
taken as written
GER is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word is used, here its opening letter

parts.note: the initial letter of this word

explanation.surface: The setter reveals his German nationality, to the surprise of office workers scanning papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Docs reads as documents being scanned, but it can also mean doctors who do medical scans.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagers are devices or people producing images, so scanners of documents or patients are imagers.

clue.text: Current Tory party? Half-hearted mob of little amount

indicators.note: half of the heart, the doubled middle, is removed

parts.note: something current is fashionable, or in
CON is the abbreviation for Conservative
a party in a dispute is a side
a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A modern Conservative gathering is a half-hearted crowd of little consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-hearted takes away one of the two letters at the heart of the crowd word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderable means small or insignificant, describing a quantity too slight to be worth considering.
